intro: Welcome back! You can already tell a story with the past simple and the past continuous. Now you'll learn to go back to something that happened even earlier, with had + the third form: When I arrived, the film had started (it started before I got there).
teachingNotes: Builds on: the third form (past participle) from a2-present-perfect-intro (have/has + third form), the past simple (regular and irregular) and past simple vs past continuous with when/while (b1-past-continuous). Form: had + third form, the SAME for every person (no 'has', no -s); short form 'd (I'd forgotten: before a third form 'd = had; the learner knows I'd like = would); negative hadn't + third form; question Had you … + third form? Common error: the past form after had (*'She had forgot her bag' → 'forgotten'; *'had went' → 'had gone'). Useful irregular third forms: gone, seen, eaten, forgotten, taken, written, fallen, begun; same as the past: left, lost, had, made, bought.

Core idea: the past perfect is the EARLIER of two past events; the past simple tells the story, had + third form goes back to something that happened before it. The heart of the lesson is this contrast: 'When I arrived, the film had started' (it started before I arrived; I missed the beginning) vs 'When I arrived, the film started' (it started at that moment). With 'when', the tense alone shows the order, so picture a timeline. If the learner asks about 'When I arrived, they were having dinner' (past continuous = already in the middle), confirm it, but don't test a three-way choice.

Indonesian trap: 'sudah'. Now → have/has (already) + third form (Saya sudah makan → I've already eaten). In a past story → had (already) + third form (Waktu Rina menelepon, saya sudah makan → When Rina called, I had already eaten; Waktu saya sampai, filmnya sudah mulai → the film had already started). The typical error drops 'had': *'When I arrived, the film already started' → 'had already started'. 'already' goes between had and the third form.

Time linkers: 'by the time' + past simple, and the other part (finished before that moment) in the past perfect: By the time we got to the restaurant, the kitchen had closed. Test this. 'before' and 'after' already show the order, so the past simple is ALSO correct there (After I had finished / After I finished my work, I went home; I had sent / I sent the email before my boss called): accept both and never make before/after sentences an either-or question. 'by + a time' (By 9 o'clock everyone had arrived) works the same way.

Don't overuse it: one past event on its own, or events told in the order they happened, take the past simple (*'Yesterday I had gone to the market' → 'Yesterday I went to the market'; 'I got up, had a shower and went to work'). 'A long time ago' is not a reason for the past perfect (In 2010 my family moved to Jakarta). 'had' alone is just the past of have (I had a meeting, I had lunch); 'had had' (I had had breakfast) is correct but rare: explain only if asked.

Limits: no past perfect continuous (had been -ing), no third conditional (if I had known), no reported speech (she said she had …), no passive (had been done). Don't teach 'before + past perfect' for an action that wasn't completed. American 'had gotten' vs British 'had got': mention only if it comes up.

keyPoints.title: had + the third form
keyPoints.explanation: The past perfect is had + the third form (past participle), the same form you know from the present perfect (I've seen). had is the same for every person: I had, she had, they had. Short form: I'd, she'd. Negative: hadn't + third form. After had, use the third form, not the past: She had forgotten her bag (not 'had forgot'); had gone (not 'had went').

examples.id: Kami belum melihat email itu (saat itu).

id.title: had + bentuk ketiga
id.explanation: Past perfect adalah had + bentuk ketiga (past participle), bentuk yang sama yang kamu kenal dari present perfect (I've seen). had sama untuk semua orang: I had, she had, they had. Bentuk pendek: I'd, she'd. Negatif: hadn't + bentuk ketiga. Setelah had, pakai bentuk ketiga, bukan bentuk lampau: She had forgotten her bag (bukan 'had forgot'); had gone (bukan 'had went').

keyPoints.title: The earlier of two past events
keyPoints.explanation: In a past story, the past simple tells what happened and had + third form goes back to something that happened before it. When I arrived, the film had started = it started first, then I arrived. When I arrived, the film started = it started at that moment. Indonesian 'sudah' in a past story → had (already). One past event on its own stays in the past simple: Yesterday I went to the market (not 'had gone').

examples.id: Waktu saya sampai, filmnya sudah mulai.

examples.en: When I arrived, the film started.

id.title: Kejadian yang lebih dulu dari dua kejadian lampau
id.explanation: Dalam cerita lampau, past simple menceritakan apa yang terjadi, dan had + bentuk ketiga kembali ke sesuatu yang terjadi sebelumnya. When I arrived, the film had started = filmnya mulai dulu, baru saya sampai. When I arrived, the film started = filmnya mulai tepat saat itu. 'sudah' dalam cerita lampau → had (already). Satu kejadian lampau saja tetap memakai past simple: Yesterday I went to the market (bukan 'had gone').

keyPoints.title: by the time, before, after
keyPoints.explanation: by the time + past simple; the part that was already finished at that moment takes had + third form: By the time we got to the restaurant, the kitchen had closed. before and after already show the order, so the past simple is also correct there: After I had finished my work, I went home = After I finished my work, I went home.

blocks.text:
Quick recap: you know the **third form** of a verb (the **past participle**) from the present perfect: *I **have seen** it. She **has finished**.* The **past perfect** uses the same third form, with **had** in front:

**had + third form** → *I **had seen** it. She **had finished**. They **had gone** out.*

**had** is the same for **every** person: *I had, you had, he had, she had, we had, they had*. No *has*, no -s. The short form is **'d**: *I'd seen, she'd gone*. (You know *I'd like* = I would like. When **'d** comes before a third form, it means **had**.)
- Negative: **hadn't** (= had not) + third form: *We **hadn't seen** the email.*
- Question: **Had** + person + third form?: ***Had** you **met** him before?*

**Regular verbs** (the -ed verbs): the third form looks the same as the past: *finish → finished → **finished***. Many **irregular verbs** have a different third form. There's no rule for these, you just have to remember them: *go → went → **gone***, *forget → forgot → **forgotten***.

id.text:
Ingat lagi: kamu sudah kenal **bentuk ketiga** kata kerja (**past participle**) dari present perfect: *I **have seen** it. She **has finished**.* **Past perfect** memakai bentuk ketiga yang sama, dengan **had** di depannya:

**had + bentuk ketiga** → *I **had seen** it. She **had finished**. They **had gone** out.*

**had** sama untuk **semua** orang: *I had, you had, he had, she had, we had, they had*. Tidak ada *has*, tidak ada -s. Bentuk pendeknya **'d**: *I'd seen, she'd gone*. (Kamu tahu *I'd like* = I would like. Kalau **'d** ada sebelum bentuk ketiga, artinya **had**.)
- Negatif: **hadn't** (= had not) + bentuk ketiga: *We **hadn't seen** the email.*
- Pertanyaan: **Had** + orang + bentuk ketiga?: ***Had** you **met** him before?*

**Kata kerja beraturan** (yang memakai -ed): bentuk ketiganya sama dengan bentuk lampau: *finish → finished → **finished***. Banyak **kata kerja tidak beraturan** punya bentuk ketiga yang berbeda. Tidak ada aturannya, jadi harus dihafal: *go → went → **gone***, *forget → forgot → **forgotten***.

blocks.text: Don't use the **past form** after **had**: *She had **forgot** her bag* ✗ → *She had **forgotten** her bag* ✓; *had **went*** ✗ → **had gone** ✓. And **had** alone is simply the past of *have*: *I had a meeting* (saya ada rapat), *I had lunch* (saya makan siang). It's the past perfect only when a **third form** follows **had**.

id.text: Jangan pakai **bentuk lampau** setelah **had**: *She had **forgot** her bag* ✗ → *She had **forgotten** her bag* ✓; *had **went*** ✗ → **had gone** ✓. Lalu **had** saja hanyalah bentuk lampau dari *have*: *I had a meeting* (saya ada rapat), *I had lunch* (saya makan siang). Itu baru past perfect kalau ada **bentuk ketiga** setelah **had**.

blocks.prompt: Pak Hasan had ___ the report the night before, so he was ready for the meeting.
blocks.explain: After had comes the third form: write → wrote → written. 'wrote' is the past form (the 'had forgot' mistake), and 'write' is the base form.

id.prompt: Lengkapi: Pak Hasan had ___ the report the night before, so he was ready for the meeting.
id.explain: Setelah had ada bentuk ketiga: write → wrote → written. 'wrote' adalah bentuk lampau (kesalahan seperti 'had forgot'), dan 'write' adalah bentuk dasar.

blocks.text:
Use the past perfect when you're telling a story in the past and you need to **go back** to something that happened **earlier**. The past simple tells the story; **had + third form** shows the event that happened **before** it.

This pair is the heart of the lesson:
- *When I arrived, the film **had started**.* → the film started **first**, then I arrived. I missed the beginning.
- *When I arrived, the film **started**.* → I arrived, and the film started **at that moment**. I saw the beginning.

One small word, **had**, changes the order of the story. With **when**, nothing else tells you the order, so the tense has to do it.

id.text:
Pakai past perfect saat kamu bercerita tentang masa lalu dan perlu **kembali** ke sesuatu yang terjadi **lebih dulu**. Past simple menceritakan kisahnya; **had + bentuk ketiga** menunjukkan kejadian yang terjadi **sebelumnya**.

Pasangan kalimat ini adalah inti pelajaran:
- *When I arrived, the film **had started**.* → filmnya mulai **lebih dulu**, baru saya sampai. Saya ketinggalan bagian awalnya.
- *When I arrived, the film **started**.* → saya sampai, dan filmnya mulai **tepat saat itu**. Saya melihat bagian awalnya.

Satu kata kecil, **had**, mengubah urutan ceritanya. Dengan **when**, tidak ada kata lain yang menunjukkan urutannya, jadi bentuk kata kerjanya yang harus menunjukkan.

blocks.text:
**sudah** in a past story → **had**. Indonesian uses *sudah* for now and for the past, but English changes:
- Now: *Saya sudah makan.* → *I've **already eaten**.* (present perfect)
- In a past story: *Waktu Rina menelepon, saya sudah makan.* → *When Rina called, I **had already eaten**.*
Don't drop **had**: *When I arrived, the film already started* ✗ → *When I arrived, the film **had already started*** ✓. **already** goes between **had** and the third form.

id.text:
**sudah** dalam cerita lampau → **had**. Bahasa Indonesia memakai *sudah* untuk sekarang dan untuk masa lalu, tapi bahasa Inggris berubah:
- Sekarang: *Saya sudah makan.* → *I've **already eaten**.* (present perfect)
- Dalam cerita lampau: *Waktu Rina menelepon, saya sudah makan.* → *When Rina called, I **had already eaten**.*
Jangan hilangkan **had**: *When I arrived, the film already started* ✗ → *When I arrived, the film **had already started*** ✓. **already** diletakkan di antara **had** dan bentuk ketiga.

blocks.prompt: When Rina got to the party, Budi had gone home. Did Rina see Budi at the party?

blocks.text:
**by the time** + past simple = 'at that moment (or earlier)'. The other part was **already finished** at that moment, so it takes **had + third form**:
*By the time we got to the restaurant, the kitchen **had closed**.* → the kitchen closed first, then we got there.

**before** and **after** already tell you the order, so here the past perfect is **optional**: the past simple is correct too.
- *After I **had finished** my work, I went home.* = *After I **finished** my work, I went home.*
- *I **had sent** the email before my boss called.* = *I **sent** the email before my boss called.*
Use **had** if you want to stress that the first thing was completely finished, but both are fine.

So the past perfect really matters with **when** and **by the time**, where the tense shows the order.

id.text:
**by the time** + past simple = 'pada saat itu (atau sebelumnya)'. Bagian yang lain **sudah selesai** pada saat itu, jadi memakai **had + bentuk ketiga**:
*By the time we got to the restaurant, the kitchen **had closed**.* → dapurnya tutup lebih dulu, baru kami sampai.

**before** (*sebelum*) dan **after** (*setelah*) sudah menunjukkan urutannya, jadi di sini past perfect **boleh dipakai, boleh tidak**: past simple juga benar.
- *After I **had finished** my work, I went home.* = *After I **finished** my work, I went home.*
- *I **had sent** the email before my boss called.* = *I **sent** the email before my boss called.*
Pakai **had** kalau kamu ingin menekankan bahwa hal pertama benar-benar sudah selesai, tapi keduanya benar.

Jadi past perfect benar-benar penting dengan **when** dan **by the time**, karena bentuk kata kerjanya yang menunjukkan urutan.

blocks.text: **by** + a time works the same way: *By 9 o'clock, everyone **had arrived**.* (Jam 9, semua orang sudah datang.) And keep **had** on the **earlier** event only: the *by the time* part stays in the past simple: *By the time we **got** there, …* (not *By the time we had got there*).

id.text: **by** + waktu juga sama: *By 9 o'clock, everyone **had arrived**.* (Jam 9, semua orang sudah datang.) Dan pakai **had** hanya untuk kejadian yang **lebih dulu**: bagian *by the time* tetap memakai past simple: *By the time we **got** there, …* (bukan *By the time we had got there*).

blocks.prompt: By the time the ojek arrived, the rain ___.
blocks.explain: by the time + past simple (arrived); the rain stopped before that → had + third form: had stopped. 'has stopped' is about now, and 'stops' is present.

id.prompt: Lengkapi: By the time the ojek arrived, the rain ___.
id.explain: by the time + past simple (arrived); hujannya berhenti sebelum itu → had + bentuk ketiga: had stopped. 'has stopped' untuk sekarang, dan 'stops' itu bentuk sekarang.

blocks.text:
The past perfect is only for going **back** to an **earlier** event. If you're telling **one** past event, or events **in the order they happened**, use the **past simple**:
- *Yesterday I **had gone** to the market.* ✗ → *Yesterday I **went** to the market.* ✓ (one event: there's nothing later to go back from)
- *I got up, had a shower and went to work.* ✓ (events in order: the past simple is enough. *had a shower* is just the past of *have*.)

'It was a long time ago' is **not** a reason for the past perfect either: *In 2010 my family **moved** to Jakarta* ✓.

Ask yourself: **is there a later past event in my story, and am I going back to something before it?** Only then use **had**.

id.text:
Past perfect hanya untuk **kembali** ke kejadian yang **lebih dulu**. Kalau kamu menceritakan **satu** kejadian lampau, atau kejadian-kejadian **sesuai urutannya**, pakai **past simple**:
- *Yesterday I **had gone** to the market.* ✗ → *Yesterday I **went** to the market.* ✓ (satu kejadian: tidak ada kejadian lain yang lebih belakangan)
- *I got up, had a shower and went to work.* ✓ (berurutan: past simple sudah cukup. *had a shower* hanya bentuk lampau dari *have*.)

'Sudah lama sekali' juga **bukan** alasan untuk memakai past perfect: *In 2010 my family **moved** to Jakarta* ✓.

Tanyakan pada dirimu: **apakah ada kejadian lampau yang lebih belakangan di ceritaku, dan apakah aku kembali ke sesuatu sebelum itu?** Hanya kalau iya, pakai **had**.

In 2010 my family moved to Jakarta.

blocks.text: Many learners use **had** for anything that feels 'finished' or for every *sudah*. But *Kemarin saya sudah ke pasar* is just one event → *Yesterday I **went** to the market*. Save **had** for the event that happened **before** another past event.

id.text: Banyak pelajar memakai **had** untuk apa saja yang terasa 'sudah selesai' atau untuk setiap *sudah*. Tapi *Kemarin saya sudah ke pasar* hanya satu kejadian → *Yesterday I **went** to the market*. Simpan **had** untuk kejadian yang terjadi **sebelum** kejadian lampau yang lain.

options: Last week I had visited my grandmother in Bogor.
Last week I visited my grandmother in Bogor.
blocks.explain: There's only one past event and nothing later to go back from → past simple: visited. 'had visited' needs another, later past event in the story.

id.explain: Hanya ada satu kejadian lampau dan tidak ada kejadian yang lebih belakangan → past simple: visited. 'had visited' butuh kejadian lampau lain yang terjadi setelahnya dalam cerita.

flashcards.back: I've already eaten. / When Rina called, I had already eaten.
… had + third form: By the time we got there, the kitchen had closed.
The order is already clear: had finished or finished, both correct.

flashcards.front: Yesterday I had gone to the market. ✗
flashcards.back: Yesterday I went to the market. ✓ (one event → past simple)

resources.title: Past perfect
resources.note: A B1–B2 grammar page with two practice tests: had + third form, the earlier of two past events, the past perfect with before, and already, just and never. It also shows one extra use (a situation that continued up to a time in the past) that goes a little beyond this lesson.

id.note: Halaman tata bahasa tingkat B1–B2 dengan dua tes latihan: had + bentuk ketiga, kejadian yang lebih dulu dari dua kejadian lampau, past perfect dengan before, dan already, just serta never. Ada juga satu penggunaan tambahan (keadaan yang berlangsung sampai suatu waktu di masa lalu) yang sedikit melampaui pelajaran ini.

resources.title: Past Perfect Tense
resources.note: A clear lesson, all in English, on when and how to use the past perfect for an action finished before another past action. engVid's page for the video has a short quiz.

id.note: Pelajaran yang jelas, seluruhnya dalam bahasa Inggris, tentang kapan dan bagaimana memakai past perfect untuk kegiatan yang selesai sebelum kegiatan lampau yang lain. Halaman engVid untuk video ini punya kuis singkat.

id.intro: Selamat datang lagi! Kamu sudah bisa bercerita dengan past simple dan past continuous. Sekarang kamu belajar kembali ke sesuatu yang terjadi lebih dulu lagi, dengan had + bentuk ketiga: When I arrived, the film had started (filmnya sudah mulai sebelum saya sampai).
suggestedQuestions: Apa bedanya 'the film started' dan 'the film had started'?
Bagaimana mengatakan 'sudah' dalam cerita tentang masa lalu?
Apakah setelah before dan after harus memakai past perfect?
Kapan saya TIDAK boleh memakai past perfect?

assessment.pastp-1: Lengkapi dengan bentuk yang tepat dari 'eat': I wasn't hungry at the party because I had already ___ at home.
assessment.pastp-2: Perbaiki kesalahannya: When I got to the office, Pak Hasan had went home.
assessment.pastp-3: Lengkapi dengan bentuk yang tepat dari 'leave': When we got to the station, the last train ___ ten minutes before, so we took an ojek home.
assessment.pastp-4: Terjemahkan ke bahasa Inggris: Waktu saya sampai di kantor, rapatnya sudah mulai.
assessment.pastp-5: Perbaiki kesalahannya: Last Sunday we had gone to Ancol with the kids.
assessment.pastp-6: Lengkapi dengan bentuk yang tepat dari 'finish': By the time the guests arrived, Rina ___ cooking.
assessment.pastp-7: Gabungkan kedua kalimat dengan by the time, dan pakai past perfect untuk kejadian yang terjadi lebih dulu: We got to the stadium. The match started before that.
